subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time to join the demo this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture a concise recap of the performance-related requirements and next steps so we can align on a Mutual Action Plan (MAP). Please see the SLO checklist below and confirm anything I missed.

High-level requirements you shared:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Burst behavior: sustain 50 reqs/sec with spikes up to 120 reqs/sec for short windows.
- Concurrency: support ~20 concurrent active users making streaming requests.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required (clients expect first tokens within 150-200ms of request).
- Throughput: batch-friendly workload for embeddings and batch requests at night (up to 2k batch items).
- Availability/SLOs: target 99.9% uptime; need fallback plan for degraded performance.

Map of immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to run an internal baseline using a matched model/sequence length and return p50/p95/p99 numbers (by 7/17). Attachment: slo_checklist.xlsx
2) FinTechCo to provide a representative prompt set + traffic shape (samples + concurrency profile) and the low-priority/high-priority prompts (by 7/16).
3) Run joint load test (Redwood + FinTechCo) with the agreed workload; share traces and telemetry (target week of 7/20).
4) Confirm decision criteria: if p95 <= 300ms and no more than 5% error rate on the workload, proceed to pilot; otherwise iterate on quantization/variant selection.

Attachments: I uploaded a short SLO checklist and the demo recording (slo_checklist.xlsx, demo-recording.mp4).

Let me know if the latency/throughput numbers above match what you expect or if we should adjust. Happy to schedule a 30-min follow-up with our SE (Dylan) to deep-dive on streaming behavior.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what we need. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 300ms p95 target is for responses up to ~128 tokens. For longer responses (~256 tokens) we can accept p95 up to 600ms but would like p50 to remain low.
- For streaming specifically, our client team measures "time-to-first-byte" (TTFB) and wants it under 200ms for typical prompts. If you can include TTFB numbers in the baseline that would be great.
- Our peak spike of 120 reqs/sec is a short-lived campaign trigger (expected < 10 minutes), but the sustained 50 reqs/sec figure is the steady-state.

We can share a prompt sample and traffic histogram by tomorrow EOD. Also looping in Priya (SRE) who will own the joint load test coordination.

Would appreciate if Dylan could join the load-test kickoff — we might have a few custom headers and streaming semantics to validate.

—Alex
Senior Product Manager, FinTechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Great — thanks Alex. Noted on the two latency bands (<=128 tokens: p95 <=300ms; ~256 tokens: p95 <=600ms). We will include TTFB in the baseline report.

Quick answers to logistics:
- I'll drop the sample SLO checklist (attached) and the demo recording to the shared drive link.
- Dylan — can you propose 2 windows for a 90-min joint load test the week of 7/20? We should plan for one daytime and one off-hours run to validate both steady-state and spike behavior.

MAP owners:
- Redwood baseline + report: Marissa (owner)
- Traffic samples + acceptance criteria: FinTechCo (owner: Alex / Priya)
- Joint load test orchestration: Dylan (owner)

Thanks — will follow up with calendar invites once we lock windows.

Best,
Marissa

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks for the summary. A few technical notes from the SE/RTE perspective before we schedule the load tests:

- To validate concurrent streaming we need to know average sequence length distribution and whether clients keep connections open between requests (session affinity). Please ask FinTechCo to include connection behavior in the traffic sample.
- For the spike scenario (120 reqs/sec), we should confirm if the spikes are uniformly distributed across endpoints or concentrated on a single route — this affects batching and kernel selection.
- We'll run two baseline configurations: (A) single-node optimized kernels with 8-bit quantization and (B) multi-node (sharded) with standard kernels. Expect to see lower p95 for (A) on short sequences but more throughput in (B).
- For telemetry, please provide request IDs and any custom headers so we can correlate traces.

I'll prepare an ops runbook for the joint test (pre-checks, expected dashboards, data capture). Planning to share that by EOD 7/16.

-Lukas
Senior Field SE | Redwood Inference
